title: Historical Antecedents & Philippine Inventions
subject: Science, Technology, and Society
description: Origins of science and technology, ancient civilizations (Sumerian, Babylonian, Egyptian, Greek, Roman, Chinese), Medieval and Modern breakthroughs, and iconic Filipino inventions.
sourceFile: STS-WK1-MTWThF A book reference in STS.pdf, STS MIDTERM REVIEWER.docx

questions.question: In ancient Greece, what were the earliest scientists called before the modern term 'scientist' existed?
options: Industrial engineers
Philosophers of nature
Royal scribes
Alchemists of steel
questions.answer: Philosophers of nature
questions.explanation: Science was originally called 'philosophy of the natural world,' and early scientists were known as philosophers of nature.

questions.question: The word 'technology' comes from which two Greek root words, and what do they mean together?
options: tekhnē ('art or craft') and -logia ('subject or interest') — practical applications of knowledge about nature
logos ('number') and phusis ('sky') — pure theoretical astronomy
klinein ('to slope') and oikos ('house') — domestic engineering
scire ('to write') and metron ('weight') — legal record-keeping
questions.answer: tekhnē ('art or craft') and -logia ('subject or interest') — practical applications of knowledge about nature
questions.explanation: Tekhnē and -logia together refer to the practical application of scientific principles to improve the human situation.

questions.question: Under CHED Memorandum Order No. 20, what is the overarching goal of the Science, Technology, and Society (STS) course?
options: To memorize chemical equations without examining social context
To engage students interdisciplinarily with S&T realities—socio-political, cultural, economic, and philosophical—so they live the good life and make ethical decisions
To train students solely in patent law and corporate finance
To replace history and philosophy with mechanical drafting
questions.answer: To engage students interdisciplinarily with S&T realities—socio-political, cultural, economic, and philosophical—so they live the good life and make ethical decisions
questions.explanation: STS links science and society through technology, cultivating reflective ethical decision-making.

questions.question: During hypothesis testing in the scientific method, what is the standard goal regarding the null hypothesis (H₀) and alternative hypothesis (H₁)?
options: Accept H₀ without running any experiment
Test experimentally to see if data supports rejecting H₀ and accepting H₁ for statistical significance
Ignore dependent variables entirely
Replace observation with personal opinion
questions.answer: Test experimentally to see if data supports rejecting H₀ and accepting H₁ for statistical significance
questions.explanation: Experiments manipulate independent variables, measure dependent variables, and test whether H₀ can be rejected in favor of H₁.

questions.question: What was the first writing system developed by the Sumerians, using word pictures and triangular symbols carved on clay with wedge instruments?
options: Hieroglyphics
Cuneiform
Quipu
Sanskrit
questions.answer: Cuneiform
questions.explanation: Cuneiform used wedge-shaped marks pressed onto wet clay tablets, then left to dry for historical and trade records.

questions.question: How did the Sumerians build the City of Uruk—considered the first true city in the world—despite lacking building stones and lumber?
options: They imported white marble from India
They mixed river mud/clay with reeds to produce sun-baked bricks
They carved dwellings directly into granite cliffs
They wove giant bamboo domes
questions.answer: They mixed river mud/clay with reeds to produce sun-baked bricks
questions.explanation: Using sun-baked mud-and-reed bricks, Sumerians erected houses, city walls, and the Great Ziggurat of Ur ('mountain of god').

questions.question: Why was the Great Ziggurat of Ur built, and who was permitted to enter its inner sanctuary?
options: As a public marketplace open to all foreign traders
As the sacred temple of their chief god, where only priests were allowed to enter
As a royal library for Roman codices
As a grain watermill powered by oxen
questions.answer: As the sacred temple of their chief god, where only priests were allowed to enter
questions.explanation: Known as the 'mountain of god,' the Ziggurat of Ur was built of sun-baked bricks as a sacred temple restricted to priests.

questions.question: For what purpose were the very first Sumerian wheels originally invented?
options: Chariot racing in Olympic arenas
Farm work and food processing (such as milling grains with wheel and axle)
Oceanic sailboat steering
Mechanical wristwatches
questions.answer: Farm work and food processing (such as milling grains with wheel and axle)
questions.explanation: The textbook notes the earliest Sumerian wheels were made for farm work and milling grains rather than transportation.

questions.question: What black sticky substance similar to asphalt did the Sumerians pour over sun-baked brick roads to smoothen them?
options: Galena
Bitumen
Potassium nitrate
Paraffin
questions.answer: Bitumen
questions.explanation: Sumerians paved roads with sun-baked bricks and bitumen to keep traffic organized even during rainy muddy seasons.

questions.question: Which engineering achievements solved river flooding and scarce water for Sumerian farms, and which legendary tiered garden was attributed to Babylonian King Nebuchadnezzar II?
options: Dikes and irrigation canals; Hanging Gardens of Babylon (for Queen Amytis)
Chinampas; Great Stupa
Aqueducts; Parthenon
Windmills; Great Wall
questions.answer: Dikes and irrigation canals; Hanging Gardens of Babylon (for Queen Amytis)
questions.explanation: Sumerians built dikes and irrigation canals for year-round farming; Nebuchadnezzar II legendarily built the Hanging Gardens for Queen Amytis (though no physical evidence has been found).

questions.question: Why was the Egyptian invention of papyrus a major improvement over Mesopotamian clay tablets?
options: Papyrus was heavier and prevented letters from ever being folded
Papyrus was lighter, thinner, less breakable, and easier to carry, store, and protect from raiders
Papyrus could only be read underwater
Papyrus did not require any ink to write upon
questions.answer: Papyrus was lighter, thinner, less breakable, and easier to carry, store, and protect from raiders
questions.explanation: Processed from Nile papyrus plants, sheets were paired with tamper-proof soot-and-chemical ink for records and correspondence.

questions.question: In ancient Egypt, why did people wear kohl around their eyes and wear wigs on shaved heads?
options: Kohl (soot/malachite + galena) prevented/cured eye diseases and warded off evil; wigs protected from sun rays, let heat escape, and prevented head lice
Both were used strictly as winter thermal insulation
Kohl was a wartime camouflage; wigs were military helmets
Both were purely modern fashion imports from Rome
questions.answer: Kohl (soot/malachite + galena) prevented/cured eye diseases and warded off evil; wigs protected from sun rays, let heat escape, and prevented head lice
questions.explanation: Ancient Egyptian cosmetics and wigs served crucial health, hygiene, and spiritual functions alongside aesthetics.

questions.question: How did the ancient Egyptian water clock (clepsydra) measure elapsed time?
options: By burning knotted silk ropes at a steady rate
By using gravity to control water flowing from one vessel to another and reading the remaining water height
By measuring shadows cast by a magnetic compass
By counting pendulum swings on a bronze gear
questions.answer: By using gravity to control water flowing from one vessel to another and reading the remaining water height
questions.explanation: The clepsydra measured elapsed time from the water level remaining as gravity drained the upper vessel.

questions.question: How did Plato's ancient Greek alarm clock signal the start of his lectures?
options: A mechanical spring rang a brass bell
Water siphoned through four vertical vessels forced trapped air out of a third vessel, creating a whistling noise
A rooster was released from a wooden cage
Hot steam spun a copper turbine
questions.answer: Water siphoned through four vertical vessels forced trapped air out of a third vessel, creating a whistling noise
questions.explanation: Plato's water-siphon alarm clock used four stacked vessels so rapid siphoning expelled air in a whistle.

questions.question: Why were Greek watermills considered superior to animal-powered mills for grinding grains?
options: They could operate in the middle of dry deserts
They required less effort and time because farmers did not need to raise animals—only access to flowing rivers
They produced electricity for Roman streetlights
They used gunpowder to spin the stones
questions.answer: They required less effort and time because farmers did not need to raise animals—only access to flowing rivers
questions.explanation: Watermills harnessed flowing water with bucketed wheels to mass-produce flour, cereals, and rice efficiently.

questions.question: Before paper became widespread in Rome, how were the first Roman newspapers—called 'gazettes'—published?
options: Printed on Gutenberg's cast-metal press
Engraved in metal or stone tablets and publicly displayed
Tied as knotted quipu strings
Painted on silk scrolls
questions.answer: Engraved in metal or stone tablets and publicly displayed
questions.explanation: Roman gazettes originally used engraved metal or stone tablets before shifting to shorthand paper editions of Senate proceedings.

questions.question: What Roman innovation, reportedly started by Julius Caesar stacking papyrus sheets and later bound with durable animal-skin covers, became the first true bound book?
options: Cuneiform tablet
Codex
Scroll
Papyrus roll
questions.answer: Codex
questions.explanation: Bound books or codices replaced bulky clay tablets and scrolls, making historical and legal record-keeping compact and durable.

questions.question: Why did the expanding Roman Empire devise Roman numerals despite earlier number systems already existing?
options: To write secret love poetry
To meet higher calculation demands from growing trade and communication across conquered territories
Because Hindu-Arabic numerals were too easy to write
To calculate planetary orbits in heliocentric models
questions.answer: To meet higher calculation demands from growing trade and communication across conquered territories
questions.explanation: Roman numerals provided a standardized counting method for empire-wide commerce and administration.

questions.question: How did ancient Chinese alchemists accidentally invent gunpowder?
options: While trying to brew black tea faster
While mixing charcoal, sulfur, and potassium nitrate in search of an elixir of immortality
While firing blue-and-white porcelain vases
While smelting iron armor for the Great Wall
questions.answer: While mixing charcoal, sulfur, and potassium nitrate in search of an elixir of immortality
questions.explanation: Instead of prolonging life, the mixture generated instant heat and gas—leading to both weapons and celebratory fireworks.

questions.question: Besides silk and the Great Wall (built to deter invaders), what Chinese invention used a wheel-based mechanism with sharp edges attached to a wooden or ceramic pot?
options: A tea-leaf shredding machine that boosted tea production and exports
A water clock for pharaohs
A mechanical calculator
A compound microscope
questions.answer: A tea-leaf shredding machine that boosted tea production and exports
questions.explanation: The Chinese tea-shredding machine enabled large-scale tea production and made China famous for tea exports alongside silk.

questions.question: How did Johann Gutenberg's 15th-century printing press improve upon earlier Chinese woodblock printing?
options: It used laser beams on papyrus
It used movable cast-metal type pressed firmly onto paper via a wooden press, spreading books rapidly even to non-writers
It required engraving every page onto stone slabs
It operated exclusively on steam power
questions.answer: It used movable cast-metal type pressed firmly onto paper via a wooden press, spreading books rapidly even to non-writers
questions.explanation: Gutenberg's cast-type press enabled mass book production and rapid dissemination of knowledge.

questions.question: What social problem during the Middle Ages spurred Zacharias Janssen to develop the first compound microscope?
options: Ship captains getting lost at sea
Population growth and polluted urbanization causing widespread illness, requiring a tool to observe tiny unseen organisms
Too many books piling up in monasteries
Spoilage of milk during train transport
questions.answer: Population growth and polluted urbanization causing widespread illness, requiring a tool to observe tiny unseen organisms
questions.explanation: Guided by earlier eyeglass principles, Janssen's compound microscope revealed microorganisms invisible to the naked eye.

questions.question: Why were the telescope, compass, oars, and rudders crucial during the Age of Exploration, and what armor solved the heavy immobility of iron plate armor?
options: They enabled safe far-distance sea navigation; chainmail
They purified river water; bitumen
They milled grain; watermills
They bound books; codex
questions.answer: They enabled safe far-distance sea navigation; chainmail
questions.explanation: Telescopes let navigators spot distant hazards and coasts; chainmail protected soldiers in close combat without the crippling weight of solid iron armor.

questions.question: What food-safety crisis led French scientist Louis Pasteur to invent pasteurization?
options: Bread turning black in wooden ovens
Dairy products (especially milk) spoiling rapidly and transmitting diphtheria, food poisoning, and typhoid fever
Saltwater lamps catching fire
Mosquitoes breeding in rice terraces
questions.answer: Dairy products (especially milk) spoiling rapidly and transmitting diphtheria, food poisoning, and typhoid fever
questions.explanation: Heating dairy products killed harmful bacteria, extending shelf life and preventing milk-borne diseases.

questions.question: Who invented kerosene ('illuminating oil') by refining petroleum when animal oil supplies could no longer meet lighting demand?
options: Alexander Graham Bell
Samuel M. Kier
Louis Pasteur
Zacharias Janssen
questions.answer: Samuel M. Kier
questions.explanation: Samuel M. Kier's refinement of kerosene established the modern petroleum refinery industry.

questions.question: Which modern inventions addressed real-time long-distance state/trade communication and rapid daily arithmetic computation?
options: Gutenberg press and clepsydra
Alexander Graham Bell's telephone and modern mechanical calculators (forerunners of computers)
Roman gazettes and abacus
Bitumen roads and plows
questions.answer: Alexander Graham Bell's telephone and modern mechanical calculators (forerunners of computers)
questions.explanation: Bell's telephone enabled real-time voice communication, while mechanical calculators paved the way for computers.

questions.question: What problem in the Philippines led Victor Llave and his team at H2O Technologies to invent the 'Salamander'?
options: Lack of rural hospital incubators
Frequent monsoon flooding making streets impassable for regular tricycles (and inter-island travel needs)
Dengue transmission by Aedes aegypti
High cost of solar batteries
questions.answer: Frequent monsoon flooding making streets impassable for regular tricycles (and inter-island travel needs)
questions.explanation: The Salamander is an amphibious tricycle capable of traversing both flooded streets and rivers or lakes.

questions.question: How does Filipina inventor Aisa Mijeno's SALt (Sustainable Alternative Lighting) lamp generate safe, non-toxic light?
options: By burning refined kerosene inside bamboo tubes
By running on saltwater (including 2 tablespoons of salt mixed in tap water), avoiding candle/kerosene fire hazards
By charging through diesel jeepney exhaust
By trapping rainwater with solar mirrors
questions.answer: By running on saltwater (including 2 tablespoons of salt mixed in tap water), avoiding candle/kerosene fire hazards
questions.explanation: The SALt lamp provides clean, fire-safe illumination for coastal and off-grid rural communities.

questions.question: How did pediatrician Dr. Fe del Mundo construct her non-electric medical incubator for premature newborns in rural areas?
options: From imported German steel and lithium batteries
By placing a smaller native laundry basket inside a larger one, inserting hot water bottles for warmth, and adding a makeshift oxygen hood
By using saltwater LEDs inside a clay pot
By converting surplus WWII jeepney engines
questions.answer: By placing a smaller native laundry basket inside a larger one, inserting hot water bottles for warmth, and adding a makeshift oxygen hood
questions.explanation: Dr. Fe del Mundo—first Asian woman admitted to Harvard Medical School—also pioneered jaundice treatment and the BRAT diet for diarrhea.

questions.question: Why did DOST-ITDI introduce the Mosquito Ovicidal/Larvicidal Trap System (OL Trap) in 2010?
options: To replace saltwater lamps in coastal towns
Because Aedes aegypti mosquitoes (dengue vectors) developed insecticide resistance and chemical sprays harmed humans and the environment
To purify drinking water in Manila
To pollinate mango trees faster
questions.answer: Because Aedes aegypti mosquitoes (dengue vectors) developed insecticide resistance and chemical sprays harmed humans and the environment
questions.explanation: The OL Trap uses natural ingredients lethal to mosquito eggs and larvae while remaining safe for people and ecosystems.

questions.question: How did the eJeepney improve upon the iconic post-WWII Filipino jeepney?
options: It added amphibious pontoons for deep ocean travel
It replaced expensive diesel engines with electricity, eliminating black smoke and exhaust noise pollution
It shrank the chassis to carry only one rider
It switched from rubber tires to wooden wheels
questions.answer: It replaced expensive diesel engines with electricity, eliminating black smoke and exhaust noise pollution
questions.explanation: Traditional jeepneys were adapted from surplus US military jeeps; eJeepneys modernize them into zero-emission urban transport.

questions.question: Which civilization built 'chinampas' (floating canal farms) and instituted mandatory education for children, and which built 'quipu' knotted-rope records and Machu Picchu?
options: Aztec; Inca
Maya; Sumerian
Egyptian; Roman
Inca; Babylonian
questions.answer: Aztec; Inca
questions.explanation: Aztecs created chinampas and mandatory education; Incas developed paved roads, Machu Picchu, suspension bridges, and quipu.

questions.question: Which Mesoamerican civilization developed Maya hieroglyphics, complex calendar systems, hydraulics, and the mathematical concept of zero?
options: Maya
Inca
Babylonian
Greek
questions.answer: Maya
questions.explanation: The Maya excelled in astronomy, calendar calculations, hydraulics, hieroglyphics, and the concept of zero.

questions.question: What is the Lebombo Bone (~35,000 BCE) from Southern Africa recognized as, and what medical system originated in ancient India?
options: The oldest known mathematical artifact; Ayurveda
A Roman surgical knife; Pasteurization
A Chinese tea shredder; Gunpowder
An Egyptian sailboat oar; Cuneiform
questions.answer: The oldest known mathematical artifact; Ayurveda
questions.explanation: Southern Africa's Lebombo Bone is the oldest known mathematical artifact; ancient India developed Ayurveda, advanced steel works, and Aryabhata's trigonometry.

questions.question: According to Chapter 1 of the STS textbook, what is the primary driving force behind the continuous, gradual improvement of science and technology across history?
options: Random entertainment without practical goals
The desire to raise the quality of life of the people in response to human needs
Avoiding all communication with neighboring societies
Eliminating agricultural production
questions.answer: The desire to raise the quality of life of the people in response to human needs
questions.explanation: Inventions build gradually on prior works out of human necessity to improve health, food, transport, safety, and daily life.
